desc:
The working schedules of all employees of a team are pooled into one list busy. Each entry [start, end] is a period in which one employee is busy (half-open: the employee is free again at time end). Periods from different employees may overlap, nest or touch.

Return the periods of common free time: the maximal ranges [a, b] with a < b in which nobody is busy. Only report gaps that lie strictly between the earliest start and the latest end of all busy periods (time before everyone has started or after everyone has finished does not count). List the gaps in increasing order. If there is no gap, return an empty array.

busy = [[1, 3], [6, 7], [2, 4], [2, 5], [9, 12]]
result = [[5, 6], [7, 9]]
constraints: The periods are in no particular order
hints: Time is common-free exactly when it is not covered by any busy period. So you need to find the holes in the union of all periods.
Sort all periods by start time and sweep, remembering the furthest end time reached so far.
When the next period starts strictly after the furthest end, the range between them is a gap. Otherwise the period extends (or is inside) the covered area: update the furthest end with max.
editorial: Merge-style sweep. Sort the busy periods by start. Keep reach, the largest end time among the periods processed so far; initially it is the end of the first period. For each next period [s, e]: if s > reach, nobody is busy during [reach, s], so record that gap; then set reach = max(reach, e). If s == reach the periods touch and no gap exists, because a gap needs positive length.

Every recorded gap is maximal: it starts where coverage stops and ends where the next period begins. Gaps come out already sorted. With sorting the algorithm takes O(n log n) time; the output needs O(n) space in the worst case.
